# QLX — Complete Reference & AI Agent Specification

> **QLX** is a type-safe, schema-first PostgreSQL query builder and executor for Go.
> Native to `pgx/v5`, zero reflection, static analysis linting, and support for PostgreSQL 16 through 19.
> This file is a complete, 100% self-contained reference. It requires no external documentation.

---

## 1. Core Architecture & Invariants

1. **Schema-First**: Your database schema (`migrations/*.sql` or a live `database_url`) is the source of truth. Running `qlx gen` inspects your schema and generates typed Go structs representing tables, columns, foreign keys, inserts, patches, enums, and scalar/set-returning functions and procedures (e.g. `db.Users`, `db.Orders`, `db.ComputeDiscount`). Views and materialized views automatically infer `NOT NULL` for columns proven non-null by their query tree (or via manual `not_null: [view.col]` in `qlx.yaml`). Simple views (or views with `INSTEAD OF` triggers) that PostgreSQL reports as updatable (`pg_relation_is_updatable`) also gain typed `Insert` and `Patch` builders for writable columns (`pg_column_is_updatable`).
2. **Zero String Construction**: SQL queries are NEVER assembled using string concatenation or raw SQL fragments (`Where("id = ?", 1)` does NOT exist). Everything is a typed Go function or method.
3. **Values vs. Expressions (`X` Suffix Rule)**:
   - Methods without `X` bind Go parameters (`$1`, `$2`): `.Eq(v)`, `.Ne(v)`, `.Gt(v)`, `.To(v)`.
   - Methods with `X` accept columns or SQL expressions: `.EqX(col)`, `.NeX(col)`, `.GtX(expr)`, `.ToX(expr)`.
4. **Immutable Builders**: Every builder method (`Where`, `OrderBy`, `Set`, `Row`, etc.) returns a new value without mutating the receiver. Always assign or chain the returned value (enforced by `qlxvet` V001).
5. **Compile-Time & Analyzer Safety**:
   - Columns are strictly typed; an integer column cannot accept a string.
   - `qlxvet` analyzer catches logical errors at build time (`V001`–`V033`, with `V027` retired): e.g. `Update` or `DeleteFrom` without `.Where(...)` or `.All()` (`V002`); `ToNull()` on a non-nullable column (`V030`); `qt.Opt[qt.Null[T]]` struct fields without `omitzero` in their `json` tag (`V031`); `OrderBy`/`Limit` on `Page` queries (`V032`); `qpage.Sorts` without `Tiebreak` (`V033`); result mapping mismatches (`V018`).
6. **Zero-Reflection Row Scanning**:
   - Use `//qlx:row` above custom result structs and run `qlx rows ./...`.
   - Generates a `ScanTargets()` method for positional scanning directly into memory pointers with zero reflection overhead.

---

## 2. CLI Workflow & Configuration (`qlx.yaml`)

### 2.1 CLI Commands

```bash
qlx init     # Write starter qlx.yaml and migrations/001_init.sql (flags: -package, -out, -dir)
qlx gen      # Read schema, write schema.lock and generated Go package (flags: -config, -from-lock)
qlx check    # CI check: fails if generated package or schema.lock is out of sync (flags: -config)
qlx verify   # Fails if a live database ($DATABASE_URL or database_url) drifted from schema.lock
qlx doctor   # Checks lock validity, config, and database_url or PostgreSQL server binaries
qlx watch    # Watches migrations and config file, regenerating on every change
qlx prepare  # Runs PREPARE on a live or throwaway server for queries dumped by qtest.Dump (-queries)
qlx rows ./... # Generates ScanTargets() methods for all //qlx:row structs in the target package (-dir)
qlx sql2go   # Converts SQL text to QLX Go code (-e "SQL", -q, -pkg; requires -tags sql2go build)
qlx regress  # Maintainer tool: translates PostgreSQL regression SQL and tracks outcomes (-tags sql2go)
```
> Note: `qlx vet` was removed (exits with code 2). Run `qlxvet` directly via `go vet -vettool=$(which qlxvet) ./...`.

### 2.2 `qlx.yaml` Reference (`qlx.yaml`, `qlx.yml`, or `qlx.json`)

Unknown keys are rejected as errors. Paths (`migrations`, `out`, `lock`) are resolved relative to the config file directory.

```yaml
package: db                      # Generated Go package name (default: db)
out: internal/db                 # Output directory (default: package name)
schemas: [public, billing]       # Schemas to generate (first = principal, unprefixed; others prefixed)
                                 # Or ['*'] for all non-empty user schemas
exclude_schemas: [audit]         # Only valid with schemas: ['*']
lock: schema.lock                # Committed schema snapshot (default: schema.lock)
migrations: migrations           # Directory of *.sql files applied to a throwaway postgres server
# database_url: postgres://...   # Live database source (wins over migrations if both set)
# pg_bin: /usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin # Directory containing postgres, initdb, pg_ctl (or $PGBIN)
targets: [16, 17, 18, 19]        # Supported PostgreSQL major versions (default: [18, 19])
exclude: [public.schema_migrations] # Tables to omit (table or schema.table)
extensions:                      # Extension packs to enable typed support for:
  - pgvector                     # Known: pgvector, postgis, pg_trgm, hstore, ltree, citext,
  - pg_trgm                      #        pgcrypto, uuid-ossp, unaccent, fuzzystrmatch, btree_gist
uuid: std                        # std (uuid.UUID) | bytes ([16]byte)
date: qt                         # qt (qt.Date) | stdlib (time.Time)
timestamptz: qt                  # qt (qt.Timestamptz, supports infinity) | stdlib (time.Time)
array_nulls: false               # true types array elements as qt.Null[T] instead of T
ids: string                      # int | string (types single-col int PKs & FKs as qt.ID[Space])
nullable: null                   # Must be "null" (qt.Null[T])
not_null:                        # View/matview columns guaranteed non-null when inference cannot prove it
  - rich_accounts.id
json_types:                      # Strongly typed JSON/JSONB columns (table.col or schema.table.col)
  users.settings: example.com/app/model.Settings
overrides:                       # Override PostgreSQL types globally or per schema.type
  numeric:
    type: github.com/shopspring/decimal.Decimal
    family: num                  # num | text | time | col
```

* **Multi-schema naming**: The first schema in `schemas` (or `public` for `['*']`) keeps unprefixed names (`Users`, `User`). All other schemas always prefix every symbol (`BillingUsers`, `BillingUser`), even without collisions.
* **Opaque IDs (`ids: string`)**: Call `qt.SetIDKey(secret)` (at least 16 bytes) once at program startup before encoding/decoding any `qt.ID`.
* **Runtime environment variables**: `DATABASE_URL` (used by `qlx verify`, `qlx prepare`, overrides `database_url`), `PGBIN` (PostgreSQL binaries directory for throwaway server).

---

## 3. Package Structure & Imports

```go
import (
    q "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx"                 // Core query builder DSL
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qt"                // Value types: Null, Opt, Date, ID, Numeric, JSONB, etc.
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/pgxexec"           // Connection, execution, bulk, pipelines, transactions, LISTEN
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qpage"             // Signed cursor pagination for service layers
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qjson"             // Strict JSON & query-string decoding for HTTP APIs
    qvalidator "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qjson/validator" // Package name is qvalidator!
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/pg"                // Flat facade for PostgreSQL built-in functions
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/pgcat/..."         // Domain packages: text, num, datetime, jsonb, network, ext/...
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/textsearch"   // Full-Text Search helpers
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/pgvector"     // Vector Search helpers (pgvector)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/trgm"         // Trigram Search helpers (pg_trgm)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/pgcrypto"     // Hashing, HMAC, random bytes, PGP encryption (pgcrypto)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/postgis"      // Spatial geography helpers (PostGIS)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/ltree"        // Hierarchical path helpers (ltree)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/hstore"       // Key-value hstore helpers (hstore)
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/otelqlx"           // Separate go.mod: OpenTelemetry tracer/metrics adapter
    "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qtest"             // Snapshot, Prepare verification, Dump, RunRegress

    "example.com/app/db"                            // Generated package containing table definitions
)
```

---

## 4. Connection, Execution & Observability (`pgxexec`, `otelqlx`)

### 4.1 Connecting & Pool Modes
```go
client, err := pgxexec.Connect(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"), pgxexec.ConnectOptions{
    Mode:         pgxexec.CacheStatements, // Default; use CacheDescribe for PgBouncer transaction mode, or Simple
    Spec:         &db.Spec,                // Target PostgreSQL versions and table fingerprints
    MinServer:    16,                      // Minimum supported PostgreSQL major version
    AfterConnect: db.RegisterTypes,        // Optional additional per-connection registration
    Tracer:       tracer,                  // Optional pgxexec.Tracer (or pgxexec.Tracers{...})
    Shapes:       qlx.DefaultShapes,       // Optional custom *qlx.ShapeCache
    OnAhead:      func(serverMajor int, targets []int) { /* server newer than Spec.Targets */ },
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer client.Close()
```
* **Dialect versions**: `qlx.Dialect{Version: qlx.PG16}` .. `qlx.PG19` (zero value defaults to newest, `PG19`). `pgxexec.Connect` auto-detects `server_version_num` and fails with `qlx.ErrUnsupportedByServer` before any network call if a query uses a feature newer than the server.
* **Schema verification at startup**:
  - `pgxexec.VerifySchema(ctx, client.DB(), db.Spec, "users", "orders")`: Checks live database tables/columns against `db.Spec` (pass table names to limit scope).
  - `pgxexec.VerifyRow[R](ctx, client.Pool, stmt, opts...)`: Asks PostgreSQL to describe a query without executing it and verifies `R` matches column count, types, and nullability (`pgxexec.AllowNullable()` option available).

### 4.2 Methods on `*pgxexec.Client`
* `client.All[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`: Returns `([]R, error)`. Returns empty slice if no rows match.
* `client.One[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`: Returns `(R, error)`. Returns `pgx.ErrNoRows` if no row matches; returns error if >1 row.
* `client.Maybe[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`: Returns `(qt.Opt[R], error)`. If no row matches, returns `qt.Opt[R]{Set: false}` and `nil` error.
* `client.Each[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`: Returns Go 1.23+ iterator `iter.Seq2[R, error]` for streaming without buffering.
* `client.Page[R](ctx, base, sorts, req, binds...)`: Runs cursor pagination via `*qpage.SortSet[R]` and returns `(qpage.Page[R], error)`.
* `client.Exec(ctx, stmt, binds...)`: Executes non-query statements. Returns `(pgconn.CommandTag, error)`.
* `client.InsertMany(ctx, base, rows, opt)`: Bulk inserts multiple rows chunked under 65,535 parameters in one transaction.
* `client.InsertManyReturning[R](ctx, base, rows, opt)`: Bulk insert collecting RETURNING columns into `[]R`.
* `client.InTx(ctx, opts, retry, func(ctx, tx *pgxexec.Tx) error)`: Runs closure in a managed transaction with automatic retry on deadlocks/serialization failures (`40001`, `40P01`).
* `client.CopyIn(ctx, st, rows)`: High-speed binary COPY (`st` is `q.CopyIn(Table, cols...)`, `rows` is `pgx.CopyFromSource` such as `pgxexec.CopyRows(...)`).
* `client.RunPipeline(ctx, &p)`: Sends a `*pgxexec.Pipeline` in one round trip.
* `client.Render(stmt)`: Renders `stmt` for `client.Dialect`, returning `(qlx.Stmt, error)`. (Use `qlx.SQL(dialect, stmt)` for `(string, []any, error)` directly.)
* `client.DB()`: Returns underlying `pgxexec.Querier` (wrapped with tracer if configured).
* `client.Close()`: Closes the connection pool.

### 4.3 Transactions (`*pgxexec.Tx`)
Transactions started with `client.InTx` receive a `*pgxexec.Tx` wrapper carrying the client's dialect, shape cache, and tracer:
* `tx.Exec(ctx, stmt, binds...)`
* `tx.All[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`
* `tx.One[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`
* `tx.Maybe[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)`
* `tx.Each[R](ctx, stmt, binds...)` (note: connection is busy until loop ends; do not run another query on `tx` inside the loop)
* `tx.Page[R](ctx, base, sorts, req, binds...)`
* `tx.InsertMany(ctx, base, rows, opt)`
* `tx.InsertManyReturning[R](ctx, base, rows, opt)`
* `tx.CopyIn(ctx, st, rows)`
* `tx.Savepoint(ctx, name, func(ctx) error)`: Partial rollback savepoint.
* `tx.Pgx()`: Underlying `pgx.Tx` for raw pgx operations if needed.

### 4.4 Pre-Rendered Static Hot-Path Handles (`NewStatic0`..`NewStatic4`)
For hot paths that avoid per-call shape cache hashing and parameter binding mistakes:

```go
idParam := q.NewParam[int64]()
var getUser = pgxexec.NewStatic1[UserSummary](
    q.Dialect{Version: q.PG18},
    q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Email).From(Users).Where(Users.ID.EqX(idParam)),
    idParam,
)

// Execution (methods: All, One, Maybe, Each, Exec, Stmt):
user, err := getUser.One(ctx, client.DB(), 42)
```
Available constructors: `NewStatic0[R]`, `NewStatic1[R, A]`, `NewStatic2[R, A, B]`, `NewStatic3[R, A, B, C]`, `NewStatic4[R, A, B, C, D]` (argument types `A..D` are inferred from the `qlx.Param` arguments).

### 4.5 Bulk Operations (`InsertMany`, `CopyIn`, `Pipeline`, `Batch`)

#### Bulk INSERT & Upsert (`InsertMany` / `InsertManyReturning`)
`InsertMany` and `InsertManyReturning` take `[]qlx.RowAssigner` (implemented by generated `*Insert` structs like `db.UserInsert` via `Assignments()`). They automatically split large slices under PostgreSQL's 65,535-parameter limit (`qlx.MaxBindParams`) and run all chunks in one transaction when called on a pool/connection (or join the existing `tx`):

```go
rows := []qlx.RowAssigner{
    db.UserInsert{Email: "a@example.com", Tier: qt.Of("pro")},
    db.UserInsert{Email: "b@example.com", Tier: qt.Of("free")},
}

// 1. Bulk insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (returns affected row count)
count, err := client.InsertMany(ctx,
    q.InsertInto(Users).OnConflict(Users.Email).DoNothing(),
    rows,
    pgxexec.BulkOptions{MaxParams: 0}) // 0 = qlx.MaxBindParams (65,535)

// 2. Bulk upsert (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE using Excluded)
_, err = client.InsertMany(ctx,
    q.InsertInto(Users).OnConflict(Users.Email).DoUpdate(
        Users.Tier.ToX(Users.Tier.Excluded()),
    ),
    rows,
    pgxexec.BulkOptions{})

// 3. Bulk insert with RETURNING (collects returned rows in chunk order)
ids, err := client.InsertManyReturning[int64](ctx,
    q.InsertInto(Users).Returning(Users.ID),
    rows,
    pgxexec.BulkOptions{})
```
- Lower `BulkOptions{MaxParams: ...}` if rows use `ToX` expressions that carry extra bound arguments.
- To build or split statements without executing them, use `base.Values(rows...)` or `base.Chunks(rows, maxParams)`.

#### Binary COPY (`CopyIn` & `CopyRows`)
For maximum throughput when `ON CONFLICT` / `RETURNING` are not needed, use PostgreSQL's binary COPY protocol (`q.CopyIn` + `pgxexec.CopyRows` or `pgx.CopyFromSlice`):

```go
st := q.CopyIn(Users, Users.Email, Users.Tier)
n, err := client.CopyIn(ctx, st, pgxexec.CopyRows([][]any{
    {"a@example.com", "pro"},
    {"b@example.com", "free"},
}))
```
- `q.CopyIn(...).Where(...).InlineArgs()` is also available; arguments in `Where` must be inlineable because `COPY` does not accept bound parameters.
- For SQL `COPY` with options (e.g. `CopyTableOut` / `CopyQueryOut` / `CopyIn`), options include `q.WithFormat(...)`, `q.WithDelimiter(...)`, `q.WithQuote(...)`, `q.WithNull(...)`, `q.WithHeader(...)`, `q.WithOnError(...)`, `q.WithRejectLimit(...)`, `q.WithLogVerbosity(...)`, `q.WithForceQuote(...)`, `q.WithForceNotNull(...)`, `q.WithForceNull(...)`.

#### Pipelines & Batches (One Round Trip)
Send multiple independent statements in a single network round trip:

```go
// Typed Pipeline (recommended): futures are populated on Run()
// Note: PipeOne/PipeAll require *R to implement pgxexec.Scannable[R] (ScanTargets: generated rows, //qlx:row, or q.TupleN)
var p pgxexec.Pipeline
idParam := q.NewParam[int64]()
getUser, _ := client.Render(q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Email).From(Users).Where(Users.ID.EqX(idParam)))
updUser, _ := client.Render(q.Update(Users).Set(Users.Tier.To("pro")).Where(Users.ID.EqX(idParam)))

userFut := pgxexec.PipeOne[db.User](&p, getUser, idParam.Bind(1))
tagFut  := pgxexec.PipeExec(&p, updUser, idParam.Bind(1))
if err := client.RunPipeline(ctx, &p); err != nil {
    return err
}
user, err := userFut.Get()
tag, err  := tagFut.Get()

// Lower-level Batch wrapper over pgx.Batch
var b pgxexec.Batch
b.Queue(st1).Queue(st2)
br, err := b.Send(ctx, client.Pool)
defer br.Close()
rows1, err := pgxexec.BatchAll[db.User](br)
one2, err  := pgxexec.BatchOne[int64](br)
// Positional scanning variants: BatchAllScan[T] / BatchOneScan[T]
```

### 4.6 `LISTEN` / `NOTIFY` (`ListenChan`)
```go
ch, err := pgxexec.NewChannel("orders_events") // validates identifier at startup
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

for n := range pgxexec.ListenChan(ctx, client.Pool, pgxexec.ListenOptions{
    Buffer:      64,
    BackoffBase: 100 * time.Millisecond,
    BackoffMax:  30 * time.Second,
    OnReconnect: func(attempt int) { /* resync missed events */ },
    OnError:     func(err error) { log.Println("listen lost:", err) },
}, ch) {
    fmt.Println(n.Channel, n.Payload, n.PID)
}
```
For a single dedicated `*pgx.Conn`, `pgxexec.Listen(ctx, conn, handler, channels...)` is also available.

### 4.7 Shape Caching & OpenTelemetry (`otelqlx`)
* **Shape Cache**: `qlx.DefaultShapes` (32,768 shapes per process) is used automatically by `Client` and `Tx`. Use `qlx.NewShapeCache(max)` for isolated caches, inspect with `.Stats()` (`Hits`, `Misses`, `Evictions`, `Size`, `Oversize`), and monitor cache thrashing via `.OnThrash(fn)`. Queries > 16 KiB are counted as `Oversize` and not cached.
* **OpenTelemetry (`otelqlx`, separate Go module)**:
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/otelqlx"

obs, err := otelqlx.New(
    otelqlx.WithTracerProvider(tp),
    otelqlx.WithMeterProvider(mp),
    otelqlx.WithQueryText(true),     // puts parameterized SQL (never values) on db.query.text
    otelqlx.WithRecordErrors(false), // off by default: PG error messages can leak row values
)
observedDB := pgxexec.Observed(pool, obs.Observe)
```
Emits spans and `db.client.operation.duration` histograms labeled by `qlx.Tagged` name (or SQL verb), `db.system.name`, `db.operation.name`, `db.query.summary`, `db.response.status_code` (SQLSTATE), and `error.type`.

---

## 5. Complete Types Catalog (`qt` Package)

QLX provides first-class Go representations for PostgreSQL data types. Never use raw `*string` or `*int` pointers for database nullability.

### 5.1 Nullability & Dynamic Arguments
- `qt.Null[T]`: Models SQL NULL.
  - `qt.Some(v)`: Non-NULL value.
  - `qt.None[T]()`: SQL NULL.
  - Methods: `.IsNull()`, `.Valid`, `.V`, `.Ptr()`, `qt.FromPtr(p)`, `.String()` (implements `fmt.Stringer`: `%v` prints `"NULL"` or formatted value; `%#v` shows struct fields).
- `qt.Opt[T]`: Models dynamic filter / PATCH argument presence or absence. Implements `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` (except `Opt[Null[T]]`).
  - `qt.Of(v)`: Field provided.
  - `qt.Unset[T]()`: Field omitted.
  - Methods: `.Set`, `.V`, `.IsSet()`, `.IsZero()`, `.String()` (implements `fmt.Stringer`: `%v` prints `"unset"` or formatted value).
- `qt.Opt[qt.Null[T]]`: Models HTTP PATCH three-state updates.
  - `qt.Unset[qt.Null[T]]()`: Omitted in JSON -> Keep database column untouched.
  - `qt.Of(qt.None[T]())`: JSON is `null` -> Update column to SQL NULL.
  - `qt.Of(qt.Some(v))`: JSON is `"val"` -> Update column to `"val"`.

### 5.2 Date & Time
- `qt.Date`: PostgreSQL `date` (days since 2000-01-01). Formats to/from JSON `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.
  - Constructors: `qt.DateOf(year, month, day)`, `qt.DateFromTime(t)`, `qt.Today(loc)`, `qt.ParseDate("2026-03-30")`.
- `qt.TimeOfDay`: PostgreSQL `time without time zone` (microsecond resolution since midnight). JSON `"15:04:05.999999"`.
  - Constructors: `qt.TimeOfDayOf(hour, min, sec, micro)`, `qt.TimeOfDayFromTime(t)`, `qt.ParseTimeOfDay("15:04:05")`.
- `qt.TimeTZ`: PostgreSQL `time with time zone` (`qt.ParseTimeTZ(...)`). Rejects offsets beyond `±15:59:59`.
- `qt.Timestamptz`: PostgreSQL `timestamptz` (stored as microsecond UTC timestamp, supports `infinity` / `-infinity`). Formats to ISO 8601 UTC.
- `qt.LocalTime`: PostgreSQL `timestamp without time zone` (distinct from `time.Time` to prevent timezone confusion; `LocalTimeInfinity`, `LocalTimeNegInfinity`, `.Time()`, `.IsInfinite()`, `.Sign()`).
- `qt.Interval`: PostgreSQL `interval` (`Months`, `Days`, `Micros`; helpers `qt.Days(n)`, `qt.Months(n)`, `qt.Duration(d)`, `qt.ParseInterval(...)`).

### 5.3 Typed Obfuscated Entity IDs (`qt.ID[Space]`)
With `ids: string` in `qlx.yaml`, integer PKs and FKs stay `bigint`/`int` in the DB and serialize as 11-character base58 strings (`"7mQp3VxK9cE"`) in JSON/URLs:

```go
// Set once at startup (at least 16 bytes):
if err := qt.SetIDKey(secret); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

type UserSpace struct{}
func (UserSpace) IDSpace() string { return "usr" }

type UserID = qt.ID[UserSpace]

// Usage:
id := qt.IDOf[UserSpace](42)
encoded := id.String() // 11-char base58 string, e.g. "7mQp3VxK9cE"
parsed, err := qt.ParseID[UserSpace](encoded)
rawInt := parsed.Int64()
```

### 5.4 Numeric & Decimals
- `qt.Numeric`: Arbitrary precision decimal for PostgreSQL `NUMERIC` / `DECIMAL` (`type Numeric string`). Avoids float rounding bugs.
  - Construct directly: `qt.Numeric("12345.6789")` (there is no `NewNumeric` function).

### 5.5 JSON Columns
- `qt.JSONB[T]`: Strongly typed JSONB column. Automatically marshals/unmarshals `T` on read and write. Implements `fmt.Stringer` (`.String()` returns compact JSON representation). Constructors: `qt.JSONOf(v)`, `qt.Raw(b)`.
- `qt.RawJSON`: Alias for `qt.JSONB[json.RawMessage]`.
- `qt.JSON[T]`: Deprecated alias for `qt.JSONB[T]`.

### 5.6 Ranges & Multiranges (PostgreSQL 14+)
- `qt.Range[T]`: PostgreSQL range (`int4range`, `numrange`, `tstzrange`, `daterange`).
  - Fields/Accessors: `.Lower`, `.Upper`, `.LowerInc`, `.UpperInc`, `.Empty`, `.Null` (and `.Lower()`, `.Upper()`, `.LowerInclusive()`, `.UpperInclusive()`, `.IsEmpty()` / `RangeReader` / `RangeWriter`).
  - Note: A nullable range column is `qt.Range[T]` with `.Null = true` rather than `qt.Null[qt.Range[T]]` so the pgx codec fills it directly.
  - Implements `fmt.Stringer` (`.String()` returns e.g. `[1,5)` or `empty`).
- `qt.Multirange[T]`: Slice `[]Range[T]`. Implements `fmt.Stringer` (`.String()` returns e.g. `{[1,3),empty}`).

### 5.7 Extension & PostgreSQL Text-Form Types
- **Extensions**:
  - `qt.Vector` (`[]float32`), `qt.HalfVector` (`[]float32`), `qt.SparseVector` (`string`) for `pgvector`.
  - `qt.Geometry` (`string`), `qt.Geography` (`string`) for PostGIS.
  - `qt.LTree` (`string`), `qt.LQuery` (`string`), `qt.LTxtQuery` (`string`) for `ltree`.
  - `qt.Hstore` (`map[string]qt.Null[string]`) for `hstore`.
- **PostgreSQL Text-Form & System Types** (named `string` types preventing cross-type mixups):
  - `qt.TSVector`, `qt.TSQuery`, `qt.Bit` (`bit`/`varbit`), `qt.Money`, `qt.XML`, `qt.JSONPath`
  - Geometry: `qt.Point`, `qt.Line`, `qt.Lseg`, `qt.Box`, `qt.Path`, `qt.Polygon`, `qt.Circle`
  - Network: `qt.MacAddr`, `qt.MacAddr8` (IP addresses `inet`/`cidr` map to `netip.Addr`/`netip.Prefix`)
  - Catalog / Internal: `qt.Char` (`byte`, PostgreSQL 1-byte `"char"`), `qt.Void` (`struct{}`, `RETURNS void`), `qt.LSN`, `qt.RegClass`, `qt.RegType`, `qt.RegProc`, `qt.RegProcedure`, `qt.RegOper`, `qt.RegOperator`, `qt.RegNamespace`, `qt.RegRole`, `qt.RegConfig`, `qt.RegDict`, `qt.RegCollation`, `qt.RegDatabase` (PG 19), `qt.Xid`, `qt.Xid8`, `qt.Cid`, `qt.Tid`, `qt.ACLItem`, `qt.OIDVector`, `qt.Int2Vector`, `qt.Oid8` (PG 19), `qt.Snapshot`, `qt.NodeTree`, `qt.RefCursor`, `qt.NDistinct`, `qt.Dependencies`, `qt.MCVList`.

### 5.8 Web-Ready JSON Serialization Contract
All `qt` types implement `json.Marshaler` and `json.Unmarshaler` (or `encoding.TextMarshaler`/`TextUnmarshaler`) cleanly without wrapper objects like `sql.NullString`:

| Type | JSON Output / Input | Benefit / Format |
|---|---|---|
| `qt.Null[T]` | `"val"` or `null` | **Zero wrapper**: unwraps directly to primitive value or `null` |
| `qt.Opt[T]` | `"val"` or omitted | Disappears completely from JSON when unset using `json:",omitzero"` |
| `qt.Opt[qt.Null[T]]` | `"val"`, `null`, or omitted | HTTP PATCH: absent = keep, `null` = SQL NULL, `"val"` = update. Requires `json:",omitzero"` (enforced by `qlxvet` V031, else `qt.ErrUnsetOptNull`) |
| `qt.Date` | `"YYYY-MM-DD"` | Pure ISO date string (`"2026-03-30"`) |
| `qt.TimeOfDay` | `"HH:MM:SS.ffffff"` | Microsecond resolution time (`"14:30:00.000000"`) |
| `qt.Timestamptz` | ISO 8601 UTC / `"infinity"` | `"2026-03-30T14:30:00Z"`; supports `"infinity"` and `"-infinity"` |
| `qt.LocalTime` | ISO 8601 without zone | `"2024-02-29T01:02:03.123456"` or `"infinity"`/`"-infinity"` |
| `qt.Interval` | ISO 8601 Duration | `"P1Y2M3DT1H"` |
| `qt.Range[T]` | Explicit JSON object | `{"lower": 1, "upper": 5, "lower_inc": true, "upper_inc": false}` |
| `qt.Numeric` | Decimal string | `"123.45"` |
| `qt.ID[Space]` | 11-char base58 string | `"7mQp3VxK9cE"` (DB stores integer, public JSON gets opaque typed ID) |
| `qt.Vector` | Array of numbers | `[0.1, 0.45, 0.89]` |

### 5.9 PostgreSQL ENUMs
PostgreSQL `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM ('free', 'pro', 'enterprise')` types are generated into `db/enums.go`:
- **Strongly Typed Go Type**: `type UserTier string`
- **Typed Constants**: `const (UserTierFree UserTier = "free", UserTierPro UserTier = "pro", ...)`
- **Ordered Labels Slice**: `var UserTierValues = []UserTier{UserTierFree, UserTierPro, ...}` preserving PostgreSQL `enumsortorder`.
- **Validation**: `func (v UserTier) Valid() bool`
- **SQL Cast Symbol**: `var UserTierType = qlx.NewPgType[UserTier]("public", "user_tier")`
- **Usage in Queries**: `Where(Users.Tier.Eq(db.UserTierPro))`; nullable columns use `qt.Null[db.UserTier]`.

---

## 6. Strict JSON & Query Decoding + Validation (`qjson`, `qjson/validator`)

### 6.1 Strict JSON Decoding (`qjson.Decode`)
Refuses unknown fields by default at the root level and inside nested wrapper types (`qt.JSONB`, `qt.Opt`, `qt.Null`, `qt.Range`, `qt.Multirange`), enforces body size limits, and returns structured `*qjson.Error` with JSON field paths (`{"code":"...","field":"...","msg":"..."}`).

```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qjson"

type CreateUserRequest struct {
    Email    string          `json:"email"`
    Nickname qt.Null[string] `json:"nickname"`
    Tier     qt.Opt[string]  `json:"tier,omitzero"`
}

func HandleCreate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    req, err := qjson.Decode[CreateUserRequest](r)
    if err != nil {
        var jerr *qjson.Error
        if errors.As(err, &jerr) {
            // Safe to serialize directly: {"code":"...","field":"...","msg":"..."}
            http.Error(w, fmt.Sprintf("field %s: %s", jerr.Field, jerr.Code), http.StatusBadRequest)
            return
        }
    }
    _ = req
}
```
(`qjson.DecodeInto` is also available when decoding into an existing struct value.)

### 6.2 Strict URL Query String Decoding (`qjson.DecodeQuery`)
Decodes `r.URL.Query()` with the same strictness (`unknown_param`, `invalid_param`, `invalid_query`). Treats empty parameters (`?q=`) as absent unless `qjson.KeepEmptyParams()` is passed. Tag priority: `query` -> `form` -> `json` -> field name. (`qjson.DecodeQueryInto` and `qjson.QueryName` are also available.)

```go
type ListUsersQuery struct {
    Tier  qt.Opt[string] `query:"tier"`
    Sort  string         `query:"sort"`
    Limit qt.Opt[int]    `query:"limit"`
}

query, err := qjson.DecodeQuery[ListUsersQuery](r) // ?tier=gold&limit=50
```

### 6.3 DTO Validation (`qjson/validator`)
Note: The import path ends in `validator`, and its Go package name is **`qvalidator`**:

```go
import qvalidator "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qjson/validator"

type UpdateUserDTO struct {
    Email     qt.Opt[string]          `json:"email" validate:"provided,email"`
    BirthDate qt.Date                 `json:"birth_date" validate:"nonzero"`
    Nickname  qt.Opt[qt.Null[string]] `json:"nickname,omitzero" validate:"provided,omitnil,max=50"`
}

v := qvalidator.New()
if err := v.Validate(dto); err != nil {
    var fieldErrors qjson.Errors
    if errors.As(err, &fieldErrors) {
        // Produces: [{"field":"email","code":"required","msg":"is required"}, ...]
    }
}
```

#### Special QLX Validation Rules & Tag Pitfalls
- `provided`: Checks that an `Opt[T]` was explicitly present in the JSON body (even if set to `null`).
- `notnull`: Checks that a `Null[T]` is not SQL NULL.
- `nonzero`: Checks that types like `qt.Date`, `qt.ID`, `qt.Timestamptz`, or `qt.Range` are not their zero-value struct. (Standard `required` evaluates the struct header and falsely passes zero-value structs!)
- `omitnil` (built into `validator/v10`): Unset `Opt[T]` and NULL `Null[T]` unwrap to a typed `nil` pointer, so `omitnil` skips absent/null values **without** skipping `""`, `0`, or `false`.
- **Never use `validate:"omitempty,..."` on `qt.Opt[string]`** when `""` should fail `min=1` — use `omitnil`.
- **Never use `json:",omitempty"` on `qt` structs** — always use `json:",omitzero"` (Go 1.24+).
- **For `qt.Opt[qt.Null[T]]` with length/range checks**, combine `provided,omitnil,...` so explicit `null` does not fail the inner rule.

---

## 7. Row Mapping, Scanning & Testing (`//qlx:row`, `qtest`)

### 7.1 Four Scanning Modes
1. **Positional Scanning (`//qlx:row`) — PREFERRED**: Zero reflection. Fields match `SELECT` columns in exact order. Run `qlx rows ./...` after adding/modifying the struct:
   ```go
   //qlx:row
   type UserSummary struct {
       ID       int64
       Email    string
       OrderNum int64
       Nickname qt.Null[string]
       Ignored  string `qlx:"-"` // Omitted from SQL scanning
   }
   ```
2. **By Name (`db:"..."` Tags)**: Used when a custom struct has no `ScanTargets()`. Uses cached reflection. Always provide explicit `db:"column_name"` tags (Go field names are not auto-converted to snake_case).
3. **Scalar**: When `R` is a single scalar (`int64`, `string`, `bool`, `time.Time`, `qt.Null[T]`), the query must select **exactly one column**.
4. **Tuples**: Inline queries returning 1 to 8 columns without declaring a struct (`q.Tuple1[A]` .. `q.Tuple8[A..H]`):
   ```go
   pairs, err := client.All[q.Tuple2[int64, string]](ctx,
       q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Email).From(Users))
   ```

> **Outer-Join Nullability Rule**: A `NOT NULL` column on the optional side of a `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, or `FULL JOIN` can be `NULL` in results. Wrap it in `q.Nullable(col)` (produces `Expr[qt.Null[T]]`) and scan into `qt.Null[T]` — `qlxvet` V018 enforces this!

### 7.2 Query Tagging, Registration & Testing (`qtest`)
* **`q.Tagged("user_by_id", stmt)`**: Prepends `/* qlx: user_by_id */ ` to SQL for logs, `pg_stat_activity`, and `otelqlx` span/metric labels.
* **`q.Register("user_by_id", stmt)`**: Package-level registration (enforced by `qlxvet` V003/V005) enabling automated checks via `qtest`:
  - `qtest.Render(t, dialect)`: Renders every registered query and checks for errors.
  - `qtest.Snapshot(t, dialect, "queries.sql", update)`: Compares rendered SQL of all registered queries against a golden file.
  - `qtest.VerifyPrepare(t, dialect, preparer)`: Asks PostgreSQL to `PREPARE`/parse every registered query against the real schema.
  - `qtest.Dump(t, dialect, "queries.json")`: Writes JSON for offline checking via `qlx prepare -queries queries.json`.
  - `qtest.RunRegress(t, cases, opts)`: Regression runner (`RegressOptions{Dialect, Normalize, Prepare, Known}`).

---

## 8. Operators, Expressions & Predicates

### 8.1 Comparisons & Predicates
- **Value comparisons** (bind `$n`): `col.Eq(v)`, `col.Ne(v)`, `col.Gt(v)`, `col.Gte(v)`, `col.Lt(v)`, `col.Lte(v)`
- **Column / Expression comparisons**: `col.EqX(other)`, `col.NeX(other)`, `col.GtX(other)`, `col.GteX(other)`, `col.LtX(other)`, `col.LteX(other)`
- **Null checks**: `col.IsNull()`, `col.IsNotNull()`
- **Booleans**: `boolCol.IsTrue()`, `boolCol.IsFalse()`, `q.Test(pred)` (turns `Pred` into `BoolExpr`)
- **Ranges & Sets**: `col.Between(min, max)`, `col.In("a", "b")`, `col.NotIn("a", "b")`, `col.Any(slice)` (`col = ANY($1)` — keeps query shape constant!), `q.InSelect(expr, subQuery)`
- **String pattern matching** (`TextExpr`): `Like`, `ILike`, `Contains`, `ContainsFold`, `HasPrefix`, `HasSuffix`, `Lower()`, `Upper()`
- **Arrays** (`ArrayExpr[E]`): `Contains(vs...)` (`@>`), `ContainedBy(vs...)` (`<@`), `Overlaps(vs...)` (`&&`), `Has(v)` (`v = ANY(arr)`), `Cardinality()`, `Sort()` (PG 18), `Reverse()` (PG 18)
- **JSON / JSONB** (`JSONExpr[T]`): `Get(key)` (`->`), `GetIdx(i)` (`-> int`), `GetText(key)` (`->>`), `Path(keys...)` (`#>`), `PathText(keys...)` (`#>>`), `Contains(rawJSON)` (`@>`), `HasKey(key)` (`?`)

### 8.2 Boolean Combinations & Dynamic Conditional Filters (`...If`)
```go
q.And(cond1, cond2, cond3)
q.Or(cond1, cond2)
q.Not(cond)
q.If(cond, pred) // Includes pred only when Go bool cond is true
```
For optional query parameters (`qt.Opt[T]`), use the `...If` operator family (omits the predicate from SQL when `Unset`):
```go
q.Select(Users.ID).From(Users).Where(
    Users.Tier.EqIf(tierOpt),
    Users.Balance.BetweenIf(minBalOpt, maxBalOpt),
    Users.Email.ContainsFoldIf(searchOpt),
)
```
Available `...If` operators: `EqIf`, `NeIf`, `GtIf`, `GteIf`, `LtIf`, `LteIf`, `BetweenIf`, `InIf`, `IsNullIf`, `ContainsIf`, `ContainsFoldIf`, `HasPrefixIf`, `HasSuffixIf`, `LikeIf`, `ILikeIf`.

### 8.3 Expressions, Case, Casts, Null Helpers & Typed Params
- **Values & Params**:
  - `q.Val(v)`: Wraps a Go value as a typed SQL expression `Expr[T]`.
  - `p := q.NewParam[int64]()`: Creates a reusable placeholder (`col.EqX(p)`), bound at execution/render time with `p.Bind(42)`.
- **CASE**:
  ```go
  q.Case[string]().
      When(Users.Balance.Gt(1000), "vip").
      WhenX(Users.Tier.Eq("pro"), q.Val("pro")).
      Else("standard") // or .ElseX(expr) or .End() -> Expr[qt.Null[string]]
  ```
- **Casts**: `q.Cast(expr, q.PgText)` (or `q.CastN` for nullable operands, `q.ArrayOf(q.PgText)` for arrays, `q.NewPgType[T](schema, name)` for custom types). Built-in symbols: `PgInt2`, `PgInt4`, `PgInt8`, `PgFloat4`, `PgFloat8`, `PgNumeric`, `PgText`, `PgBool`, `PgBytea`, `PgUUID`, `PgTimestamptz`, `PgTimestamp`, `PgDate`, `PgXML`, `PgInterval`, `PgJSONB`, `PgJSON`, `PgInet`.
- **Null helpers**:
  - `q.Coalesce(nullableExpr, fallback)` -> `Expr[T]`
  - `q.CoalesceOp(a, b)` -> `Expr[qt.Null[T]]`
  - `q.CoalesceOpDefault(a, nonNullExpr)` -> `Expr[T]`
  - `q.NullIf(a, b)` -> `Expr[qt.Null[T]]`
  - `q.Nullable(nonNullExpr)` -> `Expr[qt.Null[T]]`
  - `q.NotNull(nullableExpr)` -> `Expr[T]` (renders `error_on_null(...)` on PG 19)
  - `q.Greatest(a, rest...)`, `q.Least(a, rest...)`

---

## 9. Statements, Clauses & Advanced SQL

### 9.1 `SELECT`, Clauses & Row Locking
```go
users, err := client.All[UserSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(
        Users.ID,
        Users.Email,
        q.Count(Orders.ID).As("orders_count"),
        q.SumBig(Orders.Total).As("revenue"),
    ).
    Distinct(). // or .DistinctOn(Users.Email)
    From(Users).
    LeftJoin(Orders).On(Orders.UserID.EqX(Users.ID)).
    Where(Users.Tier.In("pro", "enterprise"), Users.DeletedAt.IsNull()).
    GroupBy(Users.ID, Users.Email).
    Having(q.Count(Orders.ID).Gt(0)).
    OrderBy(Users.CreatedAt.Desc().NullsLast()).
    Limit(20).Offset(40)) // or .FetchFirst(20).WithTies()
```
- **Row locking** (cannot be combined with `Distinct`, `GroupBy`, `Having`, aggregates, or window functions — enforced by `qlxvet` V028):
  - `.ForUpdate()`, `.ForNoKeyUpdate()`, `.ForShare()`, `.ForKeyShare()`
  - Modifiers: `.Of(Users)`, `.SkipLocked()`, `.NoWait()`

### 9.2 Joins, Aliasing, Derived Tables & `VALUES`
```go
// Inner, Left, Right, Full, Cross Joins
q.Select(...).From(Users).Join(Orders).On(Orders.UserID.EqX(Users.ID))
q.Select(...).From(Users).LeftJoin(Orders).On(...)
q.Select(...).From(Users).CrossJoin(Settings)

// Self Join with Table Aliases
u1, u2 := Users.As("u1"), Users.As("u2")
q.Select(u1.Email, u2.Email).From(u1).Join(u2).On(u1.ManagerID.EqX(u2.ID))

// Foreign Key Join Helper
u, o := Users.As("u"), Orders.As("o")
q.Select(u.Email, o.Total).From(u).Join(o).OnFK(o.FKOrdersUserIDFkey(u))

// Derived Subquery & LATERAL in FROM/JOIN
sub := q.Subquery(q.Select(Orders.UserID).From(Orders), "o")
lat := q.Lateral(q.Select(Orders.ID).From(Orders).Where(Orders.UserID.EqX(Users.ID)).Limit(1), "latest")

// Inline VALUES table (Values1..Values4)
fID, fName := q.NewField[int64]("id"), q.NewField[string]("name")
vals := q.Values2("v", fID, fName, q.Row2[int64, string]{1, "a"}, q.Row2[int64, string]{2, "b"})
```

### 9.3 Aggregates, Grouping Sets & Window Functions
```go
// Aggregates:
q.CountAll()                             // count(*) -> AggExpr[int64]
q.Count(col)                             // count(col) -> AggExpr[int64]
q.CountDistinct(col)                     // count(DISTINCT col) -> AggExpr[int64]
q.Sum(smallIntCol)                       // sum(col) -> AggExpr[qt.Null[int64]]
q.SumBig(bigIntCol)                      // sum(col) -> AggExpr[qt.Null[qt.Numeric]]
q.SumFloat(floatCol)                     // sum(col) -> AggExpr[qt.Null[float64]]
q.Avg(intCol), q.AvgFloat(floatCol)      // AggExpr[qt.Null[qt.Numeric]] / AggExpr[qt.Null[float64]]
q.Min(col), q.Max(col)                   // AggExpr[qt.Null[T]]
q.BoolAnd(b), q.BoolOr(b), q.ArrayAgg(c)
q.StringAgg(col, ", ").OrderBy(...)      // Filtered: .Filter(cond)
q.PercentileCont(0.5).WithinGroup(...)   // Ordered-set aggregates: PercentileDisc, Mode
q.Rollup(...), q.Cube(...), q.GroupingSets(q.SetOf(...)), q.GroupingFn(...)

// Window Specification & Named Windows (.Windows(nw)):
w := q.Window().
    PartitionBy(Orders.UserID).
    OrderBy(Orders.CreatedAt.Desc()).
    Rows(q.UnboundedPreceding, q.CurrentRow) // also Range(...), Groups(...), Preceding(n), Following(n)

q.Select(
    Orders.ID,
    q.RowNumber().Over(w).As("row_num"), // also Rank, DenseRank, PercentRank, CumeDist, Ntile
    q.Lag(Orders.Total).Over(w).As("prev_total"), // also LagN, LagBy, LagDefault, Lead*, FirstValue, LastValue, NthValue
    q.SumBig(Orders.Total).Over(w).As("running_total"),
).From(Orders)
```

### 9.4 Keyset Pagination & Service-Layer Cursor Paging (`qpage`)

#### Low-level keyset (`qlx.KeyAsc` / `KeyDesc`)
```go
byDate := q.KeyDesc(Users.CreatedAt)
byID   := q.KeyAsc(Users.ID)

var after q.Pred
if lastRow != nil {
    after = q.After(byDate.After(lastRow.CreatedAt), byID.After(lastRow.ID))
}

users, err := client.All[UserSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Email, Users.CreatedAt).
    From(Users).
    Where(after).
    OrderBy(q.KeyOrder(byDate, byID)...).
    Limit(20))
```

#### Service-Layer Cursor Pagination (`qpage`)
```go
var userSorts = qpage.Sorts[UserSummary](
    qpage.Sort("created", qpage.Desc(Users.CreatedAt)), // first sort is default
    qpage.Sort("email", qpage.Asc(Users.Email)),
    qpage.Tiebreak(qpage.Desc(Users.ID)),               // NOT NULL + unique (V033)
    qpage.Sizes(20, 100),                               // optional: default 20, max 100
)

// Once at startup (at least 16 bytes; pass previous secrets for zero-downtime rotation):
if err := qpage.SetSecret(secret); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
if err := qpage.CheckSecret(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

// In service layer (base SELECT must NOT have OrderBy, Limit, Offset, or FetchFirst -> V032):
page, err := client.Page[UserSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Email, Users.CreatedAt).From(Users).Where(Users.Active.IsTrue()),
    userSorts,
    qpage.Request{Sort: sort, Cursor: cursor, Size: size})
// errors.Is(err, qpage.ErrSort) / qpage.ErrCursor -> 400; qpage.ErrCursorKey -> 500
// Returns page.Items ([]UserSummary, never nil) and page.Next ("" on last page).
```
- Key columns must be `NOT NULL` and selected in the base `SELECT` under their own names.
- Without `pgxexec`: `w, err := userSorts.Window(req)` -> `sel, err := w.Apply(base)` -> execute `sel` -> `page, err := userSorts.Page(w, rows)`.

### 9.5 Safe URL Sort Parser (`q.NewSorts`)
```go
var userSorts = q.NewSorts(map[string]q.Orderable{
    "email":   Users.Email,
    "created": Users.CreatedAt,
}).Default(Users.CreatedAt.Desc()).Tiebreak(Users.ID.Asc())

order, err := userSorts.Parse(r.URL.Query().Get("sort")) // e.g. "-created,email"
q.Select(Users.ID).From(Users).OrderBy(order...)
```

### 9.6 CTEs (`WITH`, `WITH RECURSIVE`), Set Operations & Subqueries
```go
// Standard CTE (data-modifying INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with RETURNING also allowed):
counts := q.NewCTE("counts",
    q.Select(Orders.UserID.As("user_id"), q.Count(Orders.ID).As("n")).
        From(Orders).GroupBy(Orders.UserID)).Materialized() // or .NotMaterialized()

userIDField := q.NewField[int64]("user_id")
nCountField := q.NewField[int64]("n")

users, err := client.All[UserSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(Users.Email, q.RefNum(counts, nCountField).As("order_count")).
        With(counts).From(Users).
        Join(counts).On(q.RefNum(counts, userIDField).EqX(Users.ID)).
        Where(q.RefNum(counts, nCountField).Gt(5)))

// Recursive CTE (with optional SearchDepthFirst / SearchBreadthFirst / Cycle):
tree := q.Recursive("tree", anchorQuery, func(self q.CTE) q.Query {
    return stepQueryReferencingSelf
}).SearchDepthFirst("ord", Nodes.ID).Cycle("is_cycle", "path", Nodes.ID)

// Set Operations (Union, UnionAll, Intersect, IntersectAll, Except, ExceptAll):
combined := q1.UnionAll(q2)
combined = combined.OrderBy(combined.ByName(Users.Email).Asc()).Limit(50)

// Subqueries:
q.Select(Users.Email).From(Users).Where(
    q.Exists(q.Select(Orders.ID).From(Orders).Where(Orders.UserID.EqX(Users.ID))),
)
```
*(Reference helpers for CTE/table-func/VALUES columns: `q.Ref`, `q.RefNum`, `q.RefText`, `q.RefTime`, `q.RefBool`.)*

### 9.7 Table Functions & SQL/JSON + XML
- **Built-in Table Functions** (use in `From` / `Join`, always chain `.As(alias, cols...)` and optionally `.WithOrdinality(ordField)`):
  - `q.Unnest(arr)`, `q.Unnest2(arr1, arr2)`
  - `q.GenerateSeries(start, stop)`, `q.GenerateSeriesStep(start, stop, step)`, `q.GenerateSeriesTime(start, stop, intervalStep)`
  - `q.JSONBArrayElements(doc)`, `q.JSONBEach(doc)`, `q.StringToTable(s, delim)`
- **SQL/JSON Constructors & Query Functions**:
  - `q.JSONObject(q.JSONKV(...)...)`, `q.JSONObjectAgg(...)`, `q.JSONArray(...)`, `q.JSONArrayFrom(subq)`, `q.JSONArrayAgg(v)`, `q.JSONScalar(v)`, `q.IsJSON(...)`, `q.JSONParse(...)`, `q.JSONSerialize(...)`
  - `q.JSONExists(doc, path)`, `q.JSONValue(doc, path, asType)`, `q.JSONQuery(doc, path)`, `q.JSONTable(doc, path, alias, cols...)` (`Pass`, `JSONColOrdinality`, `JSONColValue`, `JSONColExists`, `JSONColQuery`, `JSONColNested`)
- **SQL/XML**:
  - `q.XMLElement`, `q.XMLAttribute`, `q.XMLConcat`, `q.XMLForest`, `q.XMLParse`, `q.XMLPI`, `q.XMLRoot`, `q.XMLSerialize`, `q.XMLExists`, `q.IsDocument`, `q.XMLTable`

### 9.8 Functions & Procedures (Built-in and User-Defined)
- **Built-in Catalog Functions**: `import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/pg"` (`pg.Lower`, `pg.Abs`, `pg.Now`, etc.) or domain packages `pgcat/text`, `pgcat/num`, `pgcat/datetime`, `pgcat/jsonb`, `pgcat/network`, `pgcat/ext/...`.
- **User-Defined Functions (`qlx gen`)**:
  - Plain scalar functions with `IN` parameters generate typed Go wrappers returning `qlx.Expr[T]` (wrapped in `qt.Null[T]` unless `STRICT`).
  - `VARIADIC` generates a Go variadic wrapper (`JoinAll(sep, parts ...qlx.Operand[string])`).
  - Default arguments generate two wrappers: omitting trailing defaults (`Greet(who)`) and all arguments (`GreetAll(who, greeting, punct)`).
  - Set-returning functions (`SETOF` scalar or `TABLE`/`OUT` columns) generate a `qlx.TableFunc` with `<Name>Columns` and `<Name>Cols`.
  - Procedures (`CREATE PROCEDURE`) generate functions returning `qlx.Command` executed via `qlx.Call(...)`.
  - Skipped by generator: `VARIADIC "any"`, variadics with defaults, `INOUT` parameters, `OUT` on non-set functions, `SETOF` composite/record without `OUT` columns.
- **Manual Escape Hatch**: `qlx.FuncCall[RetType](schema, name, args...)` and `qlx.Func(schema, name, args...)` (for table functions).

```go
q.Select(db.ComputeDiscount(Products.Price, q.Val(qt.Numeric("0.10")))).From(Products)
q.Select(db.ConcatWithSeparator(q.Val("-"), Users.FirstName, Users.LastName, Users.Email))

srf := db.GenerateSeries(q.Val(1), q.Val(10)).As("s", db.GenerateSeriesCols.Fields()...)
q.Select(q.Ref(srf, db.GenerateSeriesCols.GenerateSeries)).From(srf)

customExpr := qlx.FuncCall[string]("app", "format_label", qlx.Arg(Users.ID), qlx.Arg(q.Val("VIP")))
```

### 9.9 `EXPLAIN`, `PlanAdvice` & Utility/Session Commands
* **`EXPLAIN`**: `stmt.Explain(q.Analyze, q.Buffers, q.FormatJSON)` or `q.Explain(stmt, ...)`. Version-checked options include `Analyze`, `Verbose`, `Buffers`, `NoBuffers`, `Wal`, `Settings`, `GenericPlan` (PG 16), `Memory` (PG 17), `IO` (PG 19), `NoCosts`, `NoTiming`, `NoSummary`, `SerializeText`/`SerializeBinary` (PG 17), `FormatText`/`FormatJSON`/`FormatYAML`/`FormatXML`.
* **`PlanAdvice`** (`planadvice.go`): Typed plan hints (`q.SeqScan`, `q.IndexScan`, `q.BitmapHeapScan`, `q.DoNotScan`, `q.On(table)`, `q.OnAlias(...)`).
* **Session / Maintenance Commands**: `q.Prepare` / `q.Execute` / `q.Deallocate` / `q.DeallocateAll`, `q.DeclareCursor` / `q.FetchFrom` / `q.MoveIn` / `q.CloseCursor`, `q.SetConfig`, `q.RefreshMaterializedView`, `q.Truncate`, `q.Vacuum`, `q.AnalyzeTables`, `q.LockTable`, `q.Grant` / `q.Revoke`, `q.ResetAll`, `q.DiscardAll`.

---

## 10. Mutations (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`)

### 10.1 `INSERT` & Upsert
```go
// Single row insert with RETURNING (use .Columns(...).FromQuery(sel) for INSERT ... SELECT,
// or .DefaultValues(), .OverridingSystemValue())
newID, err := client.One[int64](ctx,
    q.InsertInto(Users).
        Row(
            Users.Email.To("bob@example.com"),
            Users.Tier.To("pro"),
            Users.Balance.To(50),
            Users.Nickname.ToNull(),
        ).
        Returning(Users.ID))

// Upsert (OnConflict / OnConflictConstraint -> DoNothing / DoUpdate / DoUpdateWhere / DoSelect [PG 19])
_, err = client.Exec(ctx,
    q.InsertInto(Users).
        Row(Users.Email.To("bob@example.com"), Users.Balance.To(50)).
        OnConflict(Users.Email).
        DoUpdate(Users.Balance.ToX(Users.Balance.Add(50))).
        Returning(Users.ID))
```

### 10.2 `UPDATE`
> **IMPORTANT**: `q.Update(Table)` requires `.Where(...)` or explicit `.All()` (enforced by `qlxvet` V002). Use `.From(...)` for `UPDATE ... FROM`.

```go
_, err := client.Exec(ctx,
    q.Update(Users).
        Set(
            Users.Balance.ToX(Users.Balance.Sub(10)),
            Users.Tier.To("enterprise"),
            Users.Nickname.ToNull(),
        ).
        Where(Users.ID.Eq(7)).
        Returning(Users.Balance)) // Users.Balance.Old() / .New() available on PG 18+

// Partial Update via Generated Patch Struct
patch := db.UserPatch{
    Tier:    qt.Of("pro"),
    Balance: qt.Of(int64(250)),
}
_, err = client.Exec(ctx, q.Update(Users).SetPatch(patch).Where(Users.ID.Eq(7)))
```

### 10.3 `DELETE`
> **IMPORTANT**: `q.DeleteFrom(Table)` requires `.Where(...)` or explicit `.All()` (enforced by `qlxvet` V002). Use `.Using(...)` for `DELETE ... USING`.

```go
_, err := client.Exec(ctx,
    q.DeleteFrom(Orders).
        Where(Orders.Status.Eq("cancelled")).
        Returning(Orders.ID))

_, err = client.Exec(ctx, q.DeleteFrom(AuditLogs).All())
```

### 10.4 `MERGE` (PostgreSQL 15+)
Constructor is `q.Merge(Target)` (NOT `MergeInto`), and branch actions are `ThenUpdate`, `ThenDelete`, `ThenDoNothing`, `ThenInsert`, `ThenInsertDefaults`:

```go
_, err := client.Exec(ctx,
    q.Merge(Users).
        Using(NewUsers).On(Users.ID.EqX(NewUsers.ID)).
        WhenMatched().ThenUpdate(Users.Email.ToX(NewUsers.Email)).
        WhenNotMatched().ThenInsert(
            Users.ID.ToX(NewUsers.ID),
            Users.Email.ToX(NewUsers.Email),
        ).
        WhenNotMatchedBySource().ThenDelete().
        Returning(q.MergeAction(), Users.ID)) // q.MergeAction() requires PG 17+
```

---

## 11. Extensions (`qext/*`)

For extension functions/operators not covered by the high-level `qext/*` helpers, use the generated catalog wrappers in `pgcat/ext/<name>`. Helpers require `CREATE EXTENSION` in migrations.

### 11.1 Full-Text Search (`qext/textsearch`)
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/textsearch"

doc := textsearch.Document("english",
    textsearch.Weighted(textsearch.A, Articles.Title),
    textsearch.Weighted(textsearch.B, Articles.Body))
query := textsearch.Web("english", q.Val(userSearchTerm)) // also Plain, Phrase, Syntax

articles, err := client.All[ArticleSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(
        Articles.ID,
        Articles.Title,
        textsearch.Rank(doc, query).As("rank"), // also RankCover
        textsearch.Headline("english", Articles.Body, query, textsearch.Highlight{
            StartSel: "<mark>", StopSel: "</mark>", MaxWords: 25,
        }).As("snippet"),
    ).
    From(Articles).
    Where(textsearch.SearchIf(doc, "english", optUserSearchTerm)). // also Search, Match
    OrderBy(textsearch.Rank(doc, query).Desc()).
    Limit(10))
```

### 11.2 Vector Similarity Search (`qext/pgvector`)
Supports `qt.Vector` and `qt.HalfVector`. Uses index-friendly operators (`L2`, `Cosine`, `NegativeInnerProduct`, `L1`), plus transaction-local tuning `SetEfSearch(n)` and `SetProbes(n)`:
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/pgvector"

matches, err := client.All[ItemMatch](ctx,
    q.Select(Items.ID, pgvector.Cosine(Items.Embedding, targetVector).As("dist")).
    From(Items).
    OrderBy(pgvector.Cosine(Items.Embedding, targetVector).Asc()).
    Limit(10))
```

### 11.3 Trigram Similarity (`qext/trgm`)
Helpers: `Similar`, `WordSimilar`, `SimilarIf`, `Distance`, `Similarity`, `SetSimilarityThreshold`, `SetWordSimilarityThreshold`:
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/trgm"

users, err := client.All[UserSummary](ctx,
    q.Select(Users.ID, Users.Name).From(Users).Where(trgm.Similar(Users.Name, "Jonathan")))
```

### 11.4 Cryptography (`qext/pgcrypto`)
Helpers (qualified with `public`): `HashPassword(pw, cost)`, `PasswordMatches(hash, pw)`, `HMAC(data, key, alg)`, `Digest(data, alg)`, `RandomBytes(n)`, `Encrypt(data, key)`, `Decrypt(data, key)`:
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/pgcrypto"

q.InsertInto(Users).Row(Users.Email.To(email), Users.PasswordHash.ToX(pgcrypto.HashPassword(q.Val(pw), 12)))
q.Select(Users.ID).From(Users).Where(Users.Email.Eq(email), pgcrypto.PasswordMatches(Users.PasswordHash, q.Val(pw)))
```

### 11.5 Spatial Geography (`qext/postgis`)
Works on `qt.Geography` (WGS84 meters, uses GIST indexes): `Point(lon, lat)`, `WithinMeters(col, p, meters)`, `DistanceMeters(a, b)`, `GeoJSON(col, digits)`.
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/postgis"

origin := postgis.Point(q.Val(2.3522), q.Val(48.8566)) // lon, lat
q.Select(Places.Name, postgis.DistanceMeters(Places.Loc, origin).As("m")).
    From(Places).Where(postgis.WithinMeters(Places.Loc, origin, 5000))
```

### 11.6 Hierarchical Paths (`qext/ltree`)
Works on `qt.LTree` / `qt.LQuery`: `IsDescendant(path, of)`, `IsAncestor(path, of)`, `Matches(path, pattern)`, `Depth(path)`.
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/ltree"

q.Select(Nodes.Path).From(Nodes).Where(ltree.IsDescendant(Nodes.Path, q.Val(qt.LTree("top.science"))))
```

### 11.7 Key-Value Hstore (`qext/hstore`)
Works on `qt.Hstore` (`map[string]qt.Null[string]`): `Get(col, key)`, `HasKey(col, key)`, `Contains(col, other)`, `Merge(a, b)`.
```go
import "github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qext/hstore"

q.Select(Items.ID, hstore.Get(Items.Attrs, "color").As("color")).
    From(Items).Where(hstore.HasKey(Items.Attrs, "color"))
```

---

## 12. Transactions, Retries & Error Classification

```go
err := client.InTx(ctx, pgx.TxOptions{
    IsoLevel: pgx.ReadCommitted,
}, pgxexec.Retry{
    Attempts: 3, // Default 5; retries deadlocks (40P01) and serialization failures (40001)
}, func(ctx context.Context, tx *pgxexec.Tx) error {
    if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
        q.Update(Accounts).Set(Accounts.Balance.ToX(Accounts.Balance.Sub(100))).Where(Accounts.ID.Eq(fromID))); err != nil {
        return err // Rolls back
    }
    if _, err := tx.Exec(ctx,
        q.Update(Accounts).Set(Accounts.Balance.ToX(Accounts.Balance.Add(100))).Where(Accounts.ID.Eq(toID))); err != nil {
        return err // Rolls back
    }
    return nil // Commits
})

// Error helpers in pgxexec:
// pgxexec.IsUnique(err, "users_email_key")
// pgxexec.IsForeignKey(err, "")
// pgxexec.IsNotNull(err, "")
// pgxexec.IsCheck(err, "")
// pgxexec.IsSerialization(err)
// pgxexec.IsNoRows(err)
```

---

## 13. Static Analyzer (`qlxvet`)

Run as a `go vet` tool (`go install github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/analyzer/cmd/qlxvet@latest`):
```bash
go vet -vettool=$(which qlxvet) -targets=16,17,18,19 ./...
```
* Flags: `-targets` (default `18,19`, keep in sync with `qlx.yaml` `targets`), `-audit` (reports all `//qlx:ignore` suppressions with V011).
* Suppress a finding with a comment on the same or previous line: `//qlx:ignore <mandatory reason>` (missing reason triggers `V010`).
* Key rule codes (`V001`–`V033`, `V027` retired):
  - `V001` discarded immutable builder; `V002` `Update`/`DeleteFrom` without `Where`/`All`; `V003`/`V005` `Register` rules; `V004` discarded `SQL`/`Render`; `V006` out-of-scope column; `V007`/`V014` aggregate/GROUP BY mismatch; `V008` missing required INSERT columns; `V009` feature newer than `-targets`; `V012`/`V013` malformed/contradictory clauses; `V015` EXPLAIN option rules; `V018` result type `R` vs SELECT columns mismatch (count, order, names, Go types, nullability); `V019`/`V020` window rules; `V021`/`V022` table function / SQL-JSON rules; `V026` conflict target/assign table mismatch; `V028` `FOR UPDATE/SHARE` with `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY`/aggregates/windows; `V029` `DISTINCT` vs `ORDER BY`; `V030` `ToNull()` on non-nullable column; `V031` `qt.Opt[qt.Null[T]]` without `json:",omitzero"`; `V032` `OrderBy`/`Limit`/`Offset`/`FetchFirst` on `qpage` base `SELECT`; `V033` `qpage.Sorts` without `Tiebreak`.

---

## 14. Strict Rules & Anti-Hallucination Checklist

When generating Go code with QLX, you **MUST** follow these rules:

1. **NEVER use string SQL fragments**:
   - ❌ `Where("status = ?", "active")`
   - ✅ `Where(Orders.Status.Eq("active"))`
2. **NEVER use `.Eq` to compare two columns**:
   - ❌ `Orders.UserID.Eq(Users.ID)`
   - ✅ `Orders.UserID.EqX(Users.ID)`
3. **NEVER use `.To` to assign an expression in UPDATE/INSERT**:
   - ❌ `Users.Balance.To(Users.Balance.Add(10))`
   - ✅ `Users.Balance.ToX(Users.Balance.Add(10))`
4. **NEVER invent `MergeInto` / `DoUpdate` / `DoInsert` on MERGE**:
   - ❌ `q.MergeInto(Users)...WhenMatched().DoUpdate(...)`
   - ✅ `q.Merge(Users)...WhenMatched().ThenUpdate(...)` / `.WhenNotMatched().ThenInsert(...)`
5. **NEVER use `qt.NewNumeric(...)`**:
   - ❌ `qt.NewNumeric("0.10")`
   - ✅ `qt.Numeric("0.10")`
6. **NEVER use Go pointers (`*string`, `*int64`) for database nullability**:
   - ❌ `type Row struct { Nickname *string }`
   - ✅ `type Row struct { Nickname qt.Null[string] }`
7. **ALWAYS wrap `NOT NULL` columns from the optional side of `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL JOIN` with `q.Nullable(...)`** and scan them into `qt.Null[T]`.
8. **NEVER perform an `Update` or `DeleteFrom` without `.Where` or `.All`**:
   - ❌ `q.DeleteFrom(Orders)`
   - ✅ `q.DeleteFrom(Orders).Where(Orders.ID.Eq(1))` or `q.DeleteFrom(Orders).All()`
9. **ALWAYS alias computed columns to match struct field names**:
   - ❌ `q.Select(q.CountAll()).From(...)` scanned into struct with `Count int64`
   - ✅ `q.Select(q.CountAll().As("count")).From(...)`
10. **ALWAYS place `//qlx:row` above custom result structs and run `qlx rows ./...`**.
11. **ALWAYS use `nonzero` instead of `required` for `qt.Date`, `qt.ID`, `qt.Timestamptz`, `qt.Range` in DTO validation**, import `github.com/noobmaisfier/qlx/qjson/validator` as `qvalidator`, use `validate:"omitnil,..."` (not `omitempty`) on `qt.Opt` PATCH fields, and `json:",omitzero"` (not `omitempty`) on `qt` struct fields.
12. **ALWAYS call `qpage.SetSecret` at startup** (and `qt.SetIDKey` if using `ids: string`), select all `qpage` sort/tiebreak key columns under their own names, and NEVER add `.OrderBy(...)` or `.Limit(...)` to the base `SELECT` passed to `client.Page` / `tx.Page` (enforced by `qlxvet` V032/V033).
